Package io.webagent4j.browser

Interface IFrame

All Superinterfaces:
IActionContext, ILocatorResolver<IElement>, IObservationSource, IVerificationContext
public interface IFrame extends IActionContext, IObservationSource
Backend-neutral live frame: a document boundary reached from a IPage or another IFrame via IPage.frame()/frame(), never a plain descendant DOM element.

An IFrame is a semantic handle, not a frozen snapshot: the frame criterion it was resolved from is re-evaluated against live browser state on every operation, so a query built from one IFrame instance keeps working correctly across frame navigation and frame replacement (a removed-then-reinserted <iframe> with the same semantic identity), and fails explicitly - never silently reusing stale content - once that identity can no longer be resolved unambiguously. This mirrors the re-resolution guarantee ILocator.reference() already gives at the element level, extended to the document boundary itself.

Frame instances are not thread-safe. Returned observations are immutable snapshots scoped only to this frame's own document, never mixed with the main page or a sibling frame.

    • navigate

      void navigate(String url)
      Navigates this specific frame to an absolute HTTP(S) URL, replacing its document.

      Uses the same URL-scheme validation as IPage.navigate(String): javascript:, file:, and data: URLs are rejected. The navigation is bounded by the same configured navigation timeout used for top-level page navigation.

    • extract

      default <T> ExtractionResult<T> extract(ExtractionRequest<T> request)
      Resolves request's source against this frame's current document to one unambiguous element and reads, converts, and validates its data - re-resolving this frame's own pending-scope chain fresh on every poll exactly like locate(io.webagent4j.locator.api.LocatorDefinition) already does, so a frame that disappears, is replaced, or becomes ambiguous mid-wait is caught the same way.

      The default implementation reports that this backend does not support extraction; a backend that does (the Playwright adapter) overrides it. Adding this default, rather than an abstract method, keeps every existing IFrame implementation source-compatible.

    • extractList

      default <T> ExtractionResult<List<T>> extractList(ExtractionRequest<T> request)
      Resolves every element request's source matches inside this frame, and reads, converts, and validates each one's data in DOM order.

      The default implementation reports that this backend does not support extraction; a backend that does (the Playwright adapter) overrides it. Adding this default, rather than an abstract method, keeps every existing IFrame implementation source-compatible.

    • extractTable

      default ExtractionResult<ExtractedTable> extractTable(LocatorDefinition source)
      Resolves source to one accessible HTML table inside this frame and reads its structure.

      The default implementation reports that this backend does not support extraction; a backend that does (the Playwright adapter) overrides it. Adding this default, rather than an abstract method, keeps every existing IFrame implementation source-compatible.

    • action

      IActionBuilder action()
      Starts a single action plan targeting elements inside this frame.

    • frame

      IFrameLocator frame()
      Starts a frame query scoped to the direct child frames of this frame's own document.

      A frame found this way is resolved strictly inside this frame: it can never accidentally match a same-named frame belonging to the main page or to a sibling frame.
